properties.name: The "you do not actually pay the RocksDB compile cost" premise is materially weaker than when it was measured: the profile switch it named as an occasional payer is now on the critical path, and it cost 33m 39s today
properties.statement:
NEW EVIDENCE ON AN OPEN QUESTION, NOT A NEW QUESTION. Anthony returned to this road on 2026-09-11 — *"I still want to get rid of rocksdb and go with a memory only solution where the graph is exported to git repo for persistence"* — and the honest thing to add is not another node but what changed under the existing one.

═══ WHAT `dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds` MEASURED ON 2026-08-24 ═══

It checked the premise before answering, and half-refuted it:

    release build of reflow2-mcp (~19 min)  — recompiled RocksDB: 0 times
    workspace test run #1 (~10 min)         — recompiled RocksDB: 0 times
    workspace test run #2 (~10 min)         — recompiled RocksDB: 0 times

and concluded, correctly: *"A cold first build, a CI cache miss, a new contributor's first `cargo build`, and **a profile switch** each pay the RocksDB cost in full — those are real and recurring. Day-to-day iteration does not, and a swap justified on day-to-day iteration would be justified on a cost that is not being paid."*

═══ WHAT 2026-09-11 MEASURED ═══

**The profile switch it named as an occasional payer is now on the critical path, and it was paid in full today.**

    cargo build --release -p reflow2-mcp --bin reflow2-mcp     33 min 39 s
      — dominated by librocksdb-sys compiling C++ from source;
        two `cc1plus` processes pegged for roughly 25 of those minutes.

And the reason the switch is no longer optional is the other half of the same day's work:

    propagate_from, 4 consecutive calls, one process, identical bytes
      debug    5851 / 5942 / 5904 / 5784 ms      (flat)
      release  1614 /   70 /   88 /   62 ms      (the memo working)
                                        -> 93x on the walk

    design_regions   12.5 s (debug)  ->  5.5 s cold / 2.0 s warm (release)

⭐ **93x, not the ~2.2x this project had previously recorded for the debug profile on other work.** `tools/reflow2-mcp-launch.sh:26` serves `target/debug/reflow2-mcp`, so every session today runs the slow one. Making reflow2 fast therefore REQUIRES shipping release, and shipping release means paying librocksdb-sys — so the cost moves out of "occasional" and into "on the path to the thing we want".

⚠️ **AND THE DEBUG BUILD IS WHY THE 93x WENT UNNOTICED.** It also produced a wrong reading earlier the same day: flat debug timings were recorded in `fact:the-walk-memo-takes-effect-on-the-daemon-path-and-not-on-plain-stdio-same-bytes-same-binary` as evidence that the memo was not taking effect. The release shape (1614 → 62) shows the memo working perfectly; in debug the walk is slow enough to bury it. That finding needs correcting, and it is noted here because the same profile caused both.

═══ THE DISK HALF, WHICH THAT NODE LEFT UNCONTESTED ═══

It recorded one cached `librocksdb-sys` build directory at **1.7 GB** and called the disk cost uncontested. Today, with both profiles built: **`target/` is 282 GB and the disk is at 99% (7.1 GB free)**, and the release build had to be run under a hard abort guard in case it filled the drive.

═══ WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE ═══

🛑 **IT STRENGTHENS ONE ARGUMENT AND ANSWERS NOTHING.** The list of what a store actually buys is unchanged — durability without a whole-document rewrite, crash consistency, larger-than-RAM — and the honest counterweight recorded on this node stands exactly as written: **bounded loss vs no loss.** A faster compile is not a durability story.

⚠️ Nor does it touch the two questions that would have to be answered first: what GUARANTEES the export if it is the only durable copy (`dec:idea-what-guarantees-the-export-if-the-export-is-the-only-durable-copy`, where the failure has already happened once in the field), and whether continuous auto-export collides with `dec:export-once-per-pr`, which is ACCEPTED.

⚠️ **AND A CHEAPER ROAD REACHES MOST OF THIS BENEFIT WITHOUT TOUCHING THE STORAGE MODEL:** serve a release binary that is rebuilt deliberately rather than per launch. That would capture the 93x and leave every durability question closed. Whether the compile and disk costs alone justify the storage inversion is exactly what nobody has decided — **five Decisions on this road have been open since 2026-08-24 and none has been settled.**
